This meant that during type conversion (in `ParamType.convert()`) or eager callbacks, the source had not yet been recorded, resulting in `None` [pr_3484#0][pr_3475#0]. 

The issue was first reported in [issue_3458](https://github.com/pallets/click/issues/3458), where the regression was demonstrated via a test case showing `get_parameter_source()` returning `None` for both default values and command-line inputs. The fix, implemented in PRs [3484](https://github.com/pallets/click/pull/3484) and [3475](https://github.com/pallets/click/pull/3475), restored the source recording to occur **after** `consume_value()` but **before** `process_value()`, mirroring the 8.3.3 behavior while preserving the arbitration logic from #3404 [pr_3484#0]. 

This change was included in the 8.4.0 release [release_8.4.0#0], and the final commit [d42f15b](https://github.com/pallets/click/commit/d42f15b71757de791a5781fb179fd972da9169f5) merged the fix.

The issue with `click.launch()` failing to open files with spaces in the name on Windows stems from improper handling of spaces in the command arguments passed to `explorer.exe`. The root cause was identified as the way arguments were formatted when using `subprocess.call`. Earlier attempts, such as in PR #3216, proposed building the command as a single string with quotes around the path (e.g., `explorer /select,"{url}"`) to ensure proper parsing by `explorer.exe` [pr_3216]. However, this PR was closed without merging. 

The resolved fix, implemented in PR #3307, addressed the issue by wrapping the path in double quotes within the argument list:  
```python
args = ["explorer", f'/select,"{url}"']
```  
This ensures the path with spaces is correctly interpreted by Windows Explorer [pr_3307]. PR #3478 also references fixing this issue but does not provide additional implementation details [pr_3478]. 

Thus, the problem was resolved by properly quoting the path in the `explorer` command arguments, as merged in PR #3307.
